answer: Roots show where hands have been. In a ledger's credit graph, accounts that sprout like walnut saplings from the same soil - shared funding hops, matching rest days, mirrored silence - form one root system no mask can shave away. An ocean of fresh signups costs a farmer little; a tundra of accounts forced to survive a slow winter without trading favors with neighbors costs nearly everything. Weigh the shape of the ties, not the number of faces.
